subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What different themes do students raise in these open responses?

judge.implied_focus: The thematic content of students' open-ended responses -- i.e. what topics/themes they raise and their valence.

per_column.name: themes
per_column.rationale: Multi-label decomposition of each response into a coherent taxonomy of themes (hands_on_missing, digital_tools_engagement, teacher_quality, etc.), directly realising the 'different themes' focus at a rich granularity.

per_column.name: primary_theme
per_column.rationale: Single dominant theme per response using the same coherent taxonomy; complements the multi-label column and enables frequency/ranking analysis of the leading theme.

per_column.name: sentiment
per_column.rationale: Valence facet (positive/mixed/negative) that adds an interpretive dimension to the themes, letting an analyst cross themes with tone rather than being a bare mechanical restatement.

judge.rationale: All three columns centre tightly on one inferable focus: the themes present in student open responses. 'themes' and 'primary_theme' share a coherent, substantive taxonomy (multi-label + dominant-label views), giving a sound analytical structure at useful granularity rather than a single restatement. 'sentiment' is a defensible added facet that enriches theme analysis (theme-by-valence) rather than being noise, though on its own bare sentiment would be weak. The implied focus is genuinely actionable -- an analyst can rank themes, examine co-occurrence, and correlate with satisfaction/role/grade. Minor deductions: sentiment is somewhat generic, and no columns tie themes to the existing satisfaction/grade structure, which would sharpen actionability further.
